dissent: The module honestly disclaims theorem status and its mismatches all fail toward 'unproved'/'counterexample', not false support; evaluating suffix_expectation on post-state 'a' (~L321) rather than prev is defensible because every decided expectation is a refusal and refused calls leave consulted journal/core fields unchanged — a premise itself enforced by the journal-mirror and nondelegated-core-changed checks.
findings: PREREQUISITE MISSING / no controls: recovered-proposals.json contains only the o21 implement entry; the module has no corruption-rejection controls (contrast check.py main()'s reject block and adapter_traces.run's changed_state/reject controls). Required discriminations (false Q invocation on refused attest, journal-only disagreement, changed actual Q generation, dropped refusal, wrong ordinal/globalindex) are never exercised, so control adequacy cannot be compared.

Charge gap: inspect_cases() runs structural() and full restore() of both traces ('s_states = restore(case['source'], False)', 'a_states = restore(case['adapter'], True)', ~L251-252) before the loop's first 'charge.take(1)' (~L265). The docstring's 'finite precharge before each inspected prefix' (~L10-14) excludes the O(events) patch replay that produces the inspected states, and the claimed total (sum over cases of len(actions)+1) is false for structural-failure cases, which are never charged. Fixture: structurally valid case with oversized event patches burns uncharged work. Minimal fix: take(1) per case before restore, or fold restore into the charged loop.

Invocation-membership gap disables the Q mask check: 'invocation-inventory' (~L275-276) only checks uniqueness and membership in actions[:i]; the next clause 'elif all(x in q_actions for x in invocations) and core.get('done') != …' (~L277) SKIPS the core-completion-mask check entirely when an invocation names a source-handled action (a_domain.source_only). Fixture: stale-complete case with 'attempt:2@15' appended to adapter invocations, rows[15].q_invoked=True, arbitrary core.done — no mismatch kind fires. Minimal fix: flag any invocation not in q_actions as its own kind and evaluate the mask unconditionally.

attest_expectation (~L146-160) is weaker than the source order in s_audit.check/s_inclusive ('source-attest' branch): it validates collected against journal append_log, while the sources compare collected to the delivered cut's own encoded fixture records and then collection[2:4] to registration/mapping. 'incomplete-registry' is unreachable and foreign-record 'incomplete-inventory' (e.g. same-head-foreign-cut shape) degrades to 'undecidable' rather than a confirmed refusal; only the registry gap is acknowledged in limitations. Direction is conservative (under-decision -> 'unproved'), but the obligation's exact-refusal coverage is not fully discharged.
limitations: Byte-level source review only; nothing was executed, so no observed run is claimed. Line anchors are approximate (packet omits numbering); function/statement quotes are exact. Incarnation-pair, publication_reply and sha256 bindings are only shape-checked in the proposal and were assessed as such. Interoperability could not be assessed because the control half is absent.
summary: NEEDS_CORRECTION. The recovered o21 artifact is a checker only: recovered-proposals.json lists 'o21-reconcile-current-implement' (reconcile_current.py, dc708c1c…) and, unlike peer obligations, no o21-*-control-build entry; the module contains no reject()/corruption controls, so checker/control interoperability is unverifiable and the wave04 boundary controls are unexercised — prerequisite missing. The checker's per-prefix journal mirror, generation coupling, invocation/mask, subclass map and suffix refusal expectations otherwise correspond to the frozen sources, but three executable defects remain: restoration is uncharged before the first take; the invocation check never requires membership in the potential-call set and silently disables the core-mask comparison when violated; and the independent attestation expectation is weaker than the source refusal order.
